title: Real Chromatic Numbers, Not a Placeholder
content: The parent file Erdos740Problem.lean defines chromaticNumber V G := Cardinal.mk V — explicitly a placeholder equal to the number of vertices, unrelated to colourings. Its open 'no_infinite_bipartite' sorry was therefore not a statement about the chromatic number at all. This file uses Mathlib's genuine SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber (ℕ∞-valued, the least number of colours in a proper colouring) and SimpleGraph.IsBipartite := Colorable 2. induce_chromaticNumber_le and bipartite_chromaticNumber_le_two are the two real structural facts: the inclusion G.induce s ↪g G is a homomorphism so χ never rises on induced subgraphs, and a bipartite graph is 2-colourable so χ ≤ 2.

title: The r = ∞ Extreme of #740 Is False
content: Erdős #740's parameter r forbids odd cycles of length ≤ r. The limit r = ∞ forbids odd cycles of every length, which is exactly bipartiteness. no_bipartite_induced_realizes_chromatic shows this extreme case fails: if χ(G) > 2, no induced bipartite subgraph H can have χ(H) = χ(G), because bipartiteness forces χ(H) ≤ 2 < χ(G). The whole obstruction is the elementary bound χ(bipartite) ≤ 2 — there is simply no bipartite subgraph of large chromatic number to find. This is the honest theorem the placeholder file's sorry was trying to express.

title: Concrete Witnesses: K₃ and Every Kₙ
content: The failure is non-vacuous. chromaticNumber_top gives χ(Kₙ) = |Fin n| = n, so the triangle K₃ already has χ = 3 > 2, and every complete graph Kₙ with n ≥ 3 has χ = n > 2. Feeding these into no_bipartite_induced_realizes_chromatic yields triangle_has_no_bipartite_realization and completeGraph_has_no_bipartite_realization: explicit graphs whose chromatic number cannot be realized on any bipartite induced subgraph. This delimits the real content of #740 to the finite-r regime, where Rödl's r = 3, 𝔪 = ℵ₀ theorem lives and the general problem stays open.
